title: Subarrays
statementMd:
Monocarp has an array 𝑎a consisting of 𝑛n positive integers. He also has a favorite integer 𝑘k (𝑘<𝑛k<n).

A sequence of consecutive elements of the array with indices from 𝑙l to 𝑟r (1≤𝑙≤𝑟≤𝑛1≤l≤r≤n) is called a subarray. Monocarp calls a subarray *𝑘k-balanced* if the following conditions hold:

- the sum of all elements in the subarray from 𝑙l to 𝑟r inclusive is divisible by 𝑘k;
- the length of this subarray is strictly greater than 𝑘k (that is, 𝑟−𝑙+1>𝑘r−l+1>k).

Help Monocarp determine the total number of 𝑘k-balanced subarrays in the array 𝑎a.

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑡t (1≤𝑡≤1041≤t≤104) — the number of test cases.

The descriptions of the test cases follow.

The first line of each test case contains two integers 𝑛n and 𝑘k (1≤𝑘<𝑛≤2⋅1051≤k<n≤2⋅105) — the number of elements in the array 𝑎a and the number 𝑘k.

The second line of each test case contains 𝑛n integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,…,𝑎𝑛a1,a2,…,an (1≤𝑎𝑖≤1091≤ai≤109) — the elements of the array 𝑎a.

Additional constraints on the input:

- the sum of 𝑛n over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅1052⋅105.

## Output

For each test case, print one integer — the number of 𝑘k-balanced subarrays in the array 𝑎a.

## Note

In the first test case of the example, the suitable subarrays are:

1. [2,1,3][2,1,3] (the sum of all elements 2+1+3=62+1+3=6 is divisible by 22);
2. [3,1,4][3,1,4] (the sum of all elements 3+1+4=83+1+4=8 is divisible by 22).

In the second test case, all elements are equal to 11, and 𝑘=3k=3. The suitable subarrays have lengths 66 and 99: there are four subarrays of length 66 and one subarray of length 99, so the answer is 55.

In the third test case, the only subarray of length strictly greater than 33 is the entire array. Its sum is 2222, which is not divisible by 33, so the answer is 00.
